title: Cross-team leads open forum notes - 2026-07-14
content:
Purpose:
This was an intentionally looser "open forum" cadence for cross-team engineering leads to surface urgent/tactical items, align on decisions that need quick cross-org input, and to call out risks for leadership escalation. Goal: leave with no more than 10 active action items and clear owners.

Attendees:
Aisha Patel (notes) — eng-serving-runtime
Marco Silva — platform-engineering
Grace Lin — observability
Jonah Kim — infrastructure
Priyanka Rao — private-deployments
Eleni Brooks — product-hosted-api (joined for rollout discussion)
Siva Narayanan — site-reliability-engineering (SRE)

Quick wins / highlights (5–10 min):
- Observability team shipped the token-cost breakdown drilldown for model routes; early usage shows 12% cost variance reduction on the test bucket (Grace).
- Private deployments: first customer completed an internal SOC review; minor doc updates only (Priyanka).
- Serving runtime: prototype for KV-prefetching at the dispatch layer landed as a perf experiment (Marco).

Metrics snapshot (shared beforehand):
- 99.92% p99 latency for aws-west-2 small tokens in last 24h (baseline SLO 99.9%).
- Avg token cost per request for top 5 customers down 6% week-over-week (Optimize recommendations + batching).
- Autoscale cold-start failures: 3 incidents in last 7 days (incident owner: Siva).

Main discussion topics (40–45 min):
1) Autoscale cold-start spike & mitigation path (SRE / infra)
- Summary: Three failures were due to container image pull timeouts + transient registry throttling during bursts. Root cause is a combination of image size and regional registry rate limits.
- Short-term mitigation agreed: add image pull retries with backoff in cluster agent + warm pool of standby nodes for the next 72-hour campaign (Jonah to run with infra ops).
- Medium-term: pursue image slimming + rebase to smaller base images (serving-runtime team to create EPIC).
- Decision: Standby node warm pool enabled for prod regions w/ high burst risk.
- Action items: Jonah -> enable warm pool (due 2026-07-16), Marco -> EPIC for image slimming and bench plan (due 2026-07-22).

2) Canary rollback policy for model rollouts (product + runtime)
- Problem: recent canary flagged quality regressions but the rollback trigger was slow (manual triage took ~45m). We need automated rollback thresholds.
- Proposal from Eleni: add a heuristic on generation quality signals (BLEU-style proxy + latency and error rate thresholds) to auto-trigger a partial rollback to the prior model variant.
- Concerns raised: false positives for short-lived noise; need human-in-the-loop confirmation for high-impact customers.
- Decision: implement auto-trigger that opens an incident and pauses traffic to the canary; require on-call confirmation for full rollback to previous variant.
- Action items: Eleni + Marco -> draft rollout policy and signal definitions (due 2026-07-21). Grace -> add the signal telemetry to the rollout dashboard (due 2026-07-21).

3) Observability retention cost vs. debugability tradeoff
- Grace presented retention options (hot-tier for 30 days, warm-tier for 90 days, archive). Product teams asked for 90-day trace retention for regressions.
- Consensus: keep 30-day default, allow 90-day by route/model via per-route opt-in with chargeback. Implementation tracked as PERF-218.
- Action items: Grace -> cost model doc for opt-in (due 2026-07-23); Marco -> API for per-route retention flag (due 2026-08-01).

4) Private deployments secure key management follow-up
- Priyanka: customers asking for HSM-backed key lifecycle APIs in Private. We need a small spec to include in upcoming Q4 RFP template.
- Discussion: align with Security team for KMS integrations and compatibility matrix.
- Action items: Priyanka -> draft brief for Sales/CS and Security (due 2026-07-20). Siva -> coordinate security review (due 2026-07-27).

Cross-cutting blockers (10 min):
- Model onboarding backlog: research team has a queue; serving-runtime capacity cannot immediately absorb large quantized models due to memory layout changes (reported by Marco).
  - Temporary workaround: prioritized onboarding for enterprise customers only; evaluate memory mapping change in next sprint.
- CI flakes on Windows-hosted artifact signing step: blocking release gating for a small set of infra PRs. Jonah to triage with Release Eng.

Decisions summary (one-liners):
- Enable prod standby warm pool for autoscale cold-start mitigation (Jonah).
- Implement auto-trigger for canary incidents; human confirmation required for full rollback (Eleni + Marco).
- Default observability retention remains 30 days; 90-day opt-in via per-route flag with chargeback (Grace + Marco).

Action items (owner — due):
- Jonah Kim — enable warm pool + run smoke test (2026-07-16)
- Marco Silva — create EPIC for image slimming + bench plan (2026-07-22)
- Eleni Brooks & Marco Silva — draft automated rollback policy and signal defs (2026-07-21)
- Grace Lin — add rollout signals to dashboard + retention cost model doc (2026-07-21, 2026-07-23)
- Priyanka Rao — HSM/KMS brief for RFP + coordinate Security review (2026-07-20, 2026-07-27)
- Siva Narayanan — follow up on autoscale incident postmortem and SRE runbook update (2026-07-18)
- Release Eng (cc: Jonah) — triage artifact signing CI flakes (2026-07-19)

Risks + asks for leadership (below the fold):
- Risk: If cold-start failures continue during marketing-driven traffic spikes, customer SLAs could be impacted. Ask: exec approval for temporary budget to maintain standby nodes for next 6 weeks if needed.
- Risk: Automated rollback heuristics could create churn if not tuned; ask: product + research support to provide labelled prompt sets for signal tuning.

Notes to self / parking lot:
- Explore lighter-weight OCI layers and delta-push for model artifacts (parking: storage team).
- Follow up on quantization memory layout changes with applied-ml (Marco to set appointment).

Next meeting prep (Aisha):
- Request short pre-reads 24h before: 1) warm pool cost estimate, 2) rollback policy draft, 3) retention cost model.
- Proposed date: 2026-07-21, same slot.

Attachments shared in Slack/Drive: links to perf dashboards, incident log INF-4927, draft dashboard screenshot (Grace).

End of notes.
